rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers mention the refusal before opening their baggage and omit the kindness they received, opening with a deliberately bitter report.
rows.anchor: gelir gelmez, daha yüklerini açmadan babalarına gördükleri ihsandan bahsetmeyerek ilk ağızda böyle acı bir haber

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turn Joseph’s conditional warning into an unqualified ban: without Benjamin, they imply, provisions will henceforth be withheld.
rows.anchor: Yûsuf’un şart ile mukayyed olan son sözünü böyle ıtlak ile öne sürerek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They hastily exaggerate the ban as though they had returned empty-handed and were wholly barred, to pressure their father into sending Benjamin.
rows.anchor: telaşlarından bu kere de boş gelmişler ve bütün bütün men‘olunmuşlar gibi mutlak bir memnû‘iyet ileri sürmüşler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s reply is an indirect rebuke: he recalls that they promised to protect Joseph, asks what became of that trust, and refuses to rely on their protection now.
rows.anchor: Onun hakkında da böyle tekidlerle وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ dediğinizde ne yaptınız?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the best protector and, when He wills to protect, preserves someone perfectly wherever they are; entrusting the son to God is better.
rows.anchor: Hıfzetmek murad edince nerede olursa olsun en hayırlı bir surette kat‘iyyen muhafaza eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob hopes that God’s mercy will protect Benjamin and spare the family another calamity.
rows.anchor: rahmetinden me’muldür ki muhafaza eder de bir musibet daha vermez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers’ first appeal happened as soon as they returned, before unloading; Joseph’s return of their capital then became a fresh inducement, as intended.
rows.anchor: evvelki sözler gelir gelmez ve yükleri açılmadan cereyan etmiş idi ve demek ki Yûsuf’un bu tedbîri ümidi vechile yeni bir müşevvik olmuştu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob will send Benjamin only after they swear by God to return him, unless all of them are surrounded, utterly defeated, and left without recourse or strength.
rows.anchor: hepiniz her cihetten mağlup olmuş, yapacak hiçbir çareniz kalmamış, hepiniz helâk olacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The severe oath and its exception seem to anticipate the later encirclement, as if Jacob had secured their lack of responsibility for that eventuality.
rows.anchor: Ya‘kūb ilerideki ihâta vaziyetini sanki ihzar etmiş ve güya o husustaki ‘adem-i mes’ûliyeti tevsik eylemiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He invokes the proverb that calamity is tied to what one says, supporting the striking fit between Jacob’s exception and later events.
rows.anchor: البلاء موكل بالمنطق belâ, dile müvekkeldir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob calls God a wakīl rather than a witness or guarantor: the role implies execution of the commitment, not testimony alone.
rows.anchor: “şâhid” veya “kefil” dememiş, “vekil” demiştir. Demek ki maksadı yalnız şehadet değil, icrâdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording supplies no proof for human suretyship in this matter; God alone is the one entrusted over everything.
rows.anchor: Ve demek ki bu babda kefâlete de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without God’s enabling help, people cannot fulfill their promises; only His power and will can carry these undertakings through.
rows.anchor: Bizim hesâbımıza bunları icrâ ediverecek kudret ve irade ancak O’nundur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reports the view that Jacob advised separate gates to avoid attracting notice as a group and suffering envy or the evil eye.
rows.anchor: ve bir haset ve gamze uğramalarından sakınmak idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob seems to have perceived a mysterious danger and prescribed a concealed tactical dispersal, like hunters spreading out.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ya‘kūb esrârengiz bir vaziyet görmüş ve buna karşı oğullarına Mısır’a girecekleri zaman avcıya dağılır gibi bir tâbiyeyi andıran sırrî bir tedbir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Precaution cannot avert what God decrees; it is still necessary as a plea for divine help and can benefit only when it accords with the decree.
rows.anchor: tedbir ile takdîr-i Hudâ’nın önüne geçilemeyeceğini anlatarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone rules; Jacob entrusts the matter to Him and teaches that believers must rely on God rather than other people or themselves.
rows.anchor: ne başkasına ne de kendilerine güvenmesinler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causal fa links the general command to trust in God to Jacob’s own reliance, indicating his prophethood and the others’ duty to follow his example.
rows.anchor: fâ-i sebebiye ile kendi tevekkülüne tefrî‘i de şâyân-ı dikkattir. Bununla kendisinin nübüvvetine işaret

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entering through the instructed gates did not avert the decree: it did not prevent the brothers’ encirclement, theft accusation, or Benjamin’s detention.
rows.anchor: ihâtaya uğramalarına, sirkatle ittiham olunmalarına, kardeşlerinin alıkonulmasına ilh. mâni‘olmadı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The precaution fulfilled Jacob’s inward need for compassionate care and servitude, relieving him of the fear that he had failed to take reasonable steps; it had no outward benefit.
rows.anchor: Bu tedbir ile gönlünün tekāzâsı def‘olmuş, nefsinde tedbirsizlikle bir kusur yapmış olmak ihtimâli bertaraf edilmiş oldu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob knew that precaution cannot defeat destiny and acted accordingly; God had taught him this through revelation, experience, or inference.
rows.anchor: böyle olacağını, yani tedbîrin takdîre mâni‘olamayacağını Ya‘kūb, biliyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people do not understand destiny: some think they control it by their plans, while others mistake trust in God for a ban on precaution.
rows.anchor: kimi kuvveti kendi tedbirlerinde zanneder, “mukadderâtımızı kendimiz tâyin edeceğiz” demeye kadar gider

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awā ilayhi means that Joseph took his brother close and drew him to his breast.
rows.anchor: Kardeşini kendine îvâ etti yanına aldı, sînesine çekti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous report describes Joseph’s hospitality: he seats the brothers in pairs, takes the solitary Benjamin to his table, then rooms with him and learns of his ten sons named after Joseph.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunur ki Yûsuf’un huzûruna girdiklerinde “işte emrettiğin biraderimiz, getirdik” diye takdim ettiler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same report says Joseph offered to replace the lost brother; Benjamin wished Joseph had shared his parents, whereupon Joseph embraced and identified himself.
rows.anchor: senin gibi bir biraderi kim bulabilir, amma ne çare ki seni Ya‘kūb ve Rahil doğurmuş değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second report says Benjamin asked never to leave Joseph; Joseph explained that detaining him would deepen Jacob’s grief and require a pretext, and Benjamin consented to the plan.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunur ki Bünyamin Yûsuf’a “artık ben senden ayrılmam” demiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph tells Benjamin not to grieve over his brothers’ past conduct or the treatment Joseph’s men will carry out, and to keep the revelation secret.
rows.anchor: bu sana anlattıklarımı kimseye sezdirme, duymamış gibi ol diye tenbih etti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting an item into a guest’s baggage while seeing him off constitutes giving it as a gift.
rows.anchor: bir müsafiri uğratırken yüküne bir şey koymak onu ona hediye etmektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Siqāya means a drinking vessel such as a cup or bowl; its definite article marks a familiar, known vessel, likely a valuable cup used in Joseph’s room.
rows.anchor: lâm-ı ahd, bunun mâlum ve ma‘hud bir meşrebe olduğunu gösteriyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reports that some described the cup as gold or silver.
rows.anchor: Nitekim bir altın veya gümüş tas idi demişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording suggests Joseph put the cup into Benjamin’s pack himself, unlike the earlier returned money; no one witnessed it, and agents were sent to turn back the caravan and search.
rows.anchor: ifadenin zâhirine nazaran Yûsuf, bunu kendi eliyle koymuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sudden public charge after their hospitality is painful; the unnamed caller is not explicitly said to be acting on Joseph’s command, though the outcome implies his authorization.
rows.anchor: Bu tâbiri Yûsuf’un emr ü telkin ettiği tasrih olunmuyor. Fakat netîce-i muâmeleye nazaran onun sevk u icâzetine iktiran ettiği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call is not truly an accusation of stealing the cup; it obliquely rebukes the brothers for abducting Joseph, while Benjamin knows the arrangement and is not offended.
rows.anchor: Hakikatte bu nidâ meşrebe için bir ittiham değil, mukaddemâ Yûsuf’u babasından kaçırmış olmalarına bir târiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph forgave his personal claim, but could not absolve their wrong against God; the rebuke was meant to prompt sincere repentance before his identity was disclosed.
rows.anchor: Yûsuf onlardan kendi hakkını affetmişti, lâkin o yaptıkları işlerde bir de hakkullah vardı ki onu afv ü mağfiret Yûsuf’un elinde değil idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This divine chastisement also secures Benjamin’s detention and fulfills the brothers’ oath’s exception that they be overwhelmed; their later tenderness confirms the repentance it prepared.
rows.anchor: bunun zımnında babalarına verdikleri taahhüd ve mîsâkın mes’ûliyetinden de kurtulacaklar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By asking what the officials seek instead of accepting the accusation and asking what was stolen, the brothers answer with refined restraint and imply that innocent people should not be accused hastily.
rows.anchor: üslûb-i hakîmâne ile nezâhetlerini beyan ve hüsn-i edebe davet yolunda şu mazmûnu ifham etmişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question also allows that the officials may simply have lost something, rather than having been robbed.
rows.anchor: ihtimal ki sizden bir şey de çalınmamıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The officials shift to saying they are missing the king’s cup and offer the finder a camel-load of provisions as a reward.
rows.anchor: Mukabilinde tekdir değil taltif

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caller switches from “we” to “I,” revealing that he leads the search party and is following Joseph’s instructions.
rows.anchor: Anlaşılıyor ki sözü o bağıran müezzin söylüyor ve evvelki cümlelerde “biz”, bunda “ben” diyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reports two glosses of suwaʿ: some take it as a measure, while others understand it as a drinking vessel like the siqāya.
rows.anchor: bazıları ölçek, bazıları da yukarıda sikāyenin bir beyânı gibi meşrebe mânasıyla tefsir etmişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reports that suwaʿ may be the noun and siqāya its descriptive attribute.
rows.anchor: sikāye vasıf olduğunu da söylemişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the verse uses the ambiguous word suwaʿ and attributes it to the king, Joseph’s wording is a deliberate double entendre; “king” could mean Joseph or the actual king, who may have gifted the cup.
rows.anchor: kaçamaklı bir tevriye kastedilmiş olduğunu anlatıyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the valuable measure used for provisioning resembled a royal standard, bystanders could take the words literally; the charge was therefore interpretable, perhaps metaphorical, rather than a false accusation.
rows.anchor: hakikatte zâhiren göründüğü gibi bir ittiham yapılmamış, kābil-i te’vîl bir tevriye kast edilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph was the state’s measure of justice and the country’s means of life; saying they were looking for a precious Joseph thrown into a well would have been terrifying.
rows.anchor: Yûsuf, devletin bir mi‘yâr-ı ma‘deleti, memleketin bir vâsıta-i hayâtı idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath particle tā functions like bā or wāw, or in their place, but additionally conveys astonishment; he favors rendering it in Turkish as “tevallahi” to retain that force.
rows.anchor: fazlaca bir de taaccüb mânası ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laqad alimtum means the officials now know the brothers’ identities and circumstances through close acquaintance, making the accusation seem astonishing.
rows.anchor: hüviyetlerimizi öğrendiniz, yakından ahvâlimize vâkıf oldunuz, cidden ilim hâsıl ettiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The officials ask the brothers to specify the applicable penalty if the missing item is found among them and their claim of innocence proves false.
rows.anchor: nezdinizde zuhur eder de bu suretle berâet iddianızda yalancı çıkarsanız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their proposed penalty is to detain, employ, or appropriate the person in whose baggage the stolen property is found; theft is an act of injustice.
rows.anchor: o malın çalınması mukabilinde sârikin kendi şahsı tutulur istihdam veya istimlâk edilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reports that under Jacob’s law the thief was handed over to the owner of the stolen property, with some commentaries specifying a term of one year.
rows.anchor: bazı tefsirlerde bir sene müddetle olduğu mezkurdur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun in “then he extracted it” refers to siqāya, not the masculine suwaʿ; the recovered object was Joseph’s cup rather than the king’s measure.
rows.anchor: zamir, “suvâ‘”a değil de “sikāye”ye ircâ‘edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That distinction matters: if the royal measure had been found, Joseph as judge would have detained Benjamin on the king’s behalf unjustly, and Benjamin might have resisted.
rows.anchor: Bu nokta mühimdir. Çünkü çıkan şey, Melik’in suvâ‘ı olmuş olsa idi Yûsuf, bir hâkim sıfatıyla kardeşini Melik nâmına zabt için hükmetmek lâzım gelecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph was claimant and investigator, while his brothers’ own proposed penalty supplied the judgment; Benjamin neither confessed nor objected, as Joseph avoided abusing his office or acting tyrannically.
rows.anchor: Yûsuf, bir müdde‘î vaziyetinde talep ve taharrî etmiş oluyor, hüküm de kardeşlerinin fetvâsıyla hakemliklerine istinad etmiş oluyordu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine stratagem was taught and arranged by God, enabling Joseph to obtain his brothers’ ruling and apply his father’s law in Egypt.
rows.anchor: ona onu Allah vahy ü tâlim eyledi de kardeşini alıkoymak için fetvâsını kardeşlerine verdirdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The king’s dīn” means Egypt’s prevailing law, especially its criminal code; theft normally brought beating and double restitution, so detention was unlawful there.
rows.anchor: Belli ki bundan maksat, o zaman Mısır memleketinde mer‘î olan şeriat ve bilhassa “cezâ kanunu”dur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph would not violate Egyptian law, and his father’s law had not yet been announced in Egypt; its courts had to apply the country’s known law.
rows.anchor: Yûsuf, hilâf-ı kanun hareketi tecviz etmeyeceği ve babasının şeriatı henüz Mısır’da ilan edilmemiş bulunduğu cihetle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prepared the circumstances and made the brothers unknowingly deliver the needed ruling, binding them by their own admission without breaching Egyptian law.
rows.anchor: kardeşlerine de işi sezdirmeyerek ol vechile cevap ve hüküm verdiriverdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The maneuver both kept Benjamin and released the other brothers from their covenant to Jacob because its exception for being overwhelmed had come to pass.
rows.anchor: öbür kardeşlerini de bâlâdaki إِلَّآ أَن يُحَاطَ بِكُمْ medlûlünde istisnâî bir vaziyete getirerek babalarına karşı verdikleri mîsâkın mes’ûliyetinden kurtardı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had the brothers deferred to Egyptian law or argued that an item in their bags proved no intentional theft, Joseph could not have achieved his aim.
rows.anchor: Yûsuf bu vesile ile matlûbuna eremeyecekti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raises whom He wills by degrees of exceptional knowledge and will; Joseph’s knowledge surpassed his brothers’ in this affair.
rows.anchor: Yûsuf’un kardeşlerine tefevvuku bir ilim tefevvukudur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: However learned a person may be, someone more knowing stands above him, and ultimately God’s knowledge is beyond all.
rows.anchor: her ilim sâhibinin fevkinde bir alîm vardır ki O, Allah’tır. O’nun ilmine kimse yetişemez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph felt the barb but concealed his hurt, endured it, and overlooked their faults; he says they are in a worse position because they are ashamed and distressed and need consolation.
rows.anchor: nefsi bu sözden bir acılık hissetmedi değil, fakat gizledi, sabretti, kusurlarına bakmadı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows their false attribution; Joseph and Benjamin know the truth and know no theft came from them.
rows.anchor: Allah, a‘lemdir. Yani ben ve kardeşim biliyoruz, ve Allah daha iyi biliyor ki hakikat sizin dediğiniz gibi değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After dropping their anger, the brothers plead for mercy and offer themselves in place of Benjamin to spare their aged father.
rows.anchor: hiddeti bırakıp şefaat ve istirham yoluna dökülerek ve aldırdıkları kardeşlerini kurtarmak için kendilerini fedâya razı olarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asaf is the most intense grief, rendered in Turkish more often by gam; in 7:150 the word also had a relation to anger.
rows.anchor: “Esef” mâlum olduğu üzere hüznün şiddetlisi demektir ki bu mânaca lisânımızda daha ziyade “gam” lafzı kullanılır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final alif either replaces the first-person yāʾ, meaning “my grief,” or lengthens a lament like “ah”; the vocative’s answer is omitted and “over Joseph” specifies its object.
rows.anchor: âhirindeki elif-i maksûre mütekellim “yâ”sından bedel, “ey esefim” demektir. Yahut nüdbe elifidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sound-play between asaf and Yusuf adds tenderness and is called tajnīs al-taṣrīf in rhetoric.
rows.anchor: “Esef” ile “Yûsuf” maddesi beynindeki cinas da kelâma ayrıca bir rikkat vermiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since yāʾ normally calls someone distant, addressing grief as if it could hear and understand is a meaningful metaphor.
rows.anchor: Esefi söz işitir, anlar kābil-i hitâb bir zât yerine koyarak nidâ ile çağırmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The loss of two more sons compounds Jacob’s separation from Joseph; he sees the brothers’ account as fabricated and does not despair, though Joseph’s bloodied shirt offered no outward sign of survival.
rows.anchor: Diğer oğullarının getirdikleri haberin de bir sanî‘a olduğunu anlıyor, ye’se inanmıyor, Allah’tan ümidini kesmiyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob imagines that Joseph would have been a kind companion in patience, and all his present calamities converge in longing for him.
rows.anchor: Yûsuf’a mukabil kendisine artık esefin kendisinden başka hemhâl olacak bir musâhib görmez oluyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report from the Messenger says Gabriel likened Jacob’s longing for Joseph to that of seventy bereaved mothers; its reward was one hundred martyrs, and Jacob never thought ill of God.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’den menkuldür ki “Ya‘kūb aleyhisselâm’ın Yûsuf’a vecdi ne dereceye bâliğ olmuştu?” diye Cebrâil’e sual etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This report shows that grief and weeping in hardship are permissible, since total self-restraint in severe distress is beyond what people can be required to do.
rows.anchor: Bu, delâlet eder ki musibet zamanında teessüf ve bükâ câizdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet wept for his son Ibrahim, saying that the heart grieves and the eye sheds tears, while they utter nothing that angers their Lord.
rows.anchor: Resûl-i Ekrem sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem de oğlu İbrâhim’e ağlamış ve “kalb hüzün duyar, göz yaş döker

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet wept at a daughter’s child; when challenged, he said only two foolish sounds were forbidden: a sound of joy and a sound of grief.
rows.anchor: “Ben sizi ağlamaktan nehyetmedim ancak iki ahmak sesten nehyettim: Biri ferah sırasında ses, biri de terah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says other communities were not given the formula “we belong to God and return to Him”; Jacob himself did not utter that formula.
rows.anchor: Muhammed ümmetinden başka ümmetlere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s eyes whitened from grief and he became blind; another report says instead that his sight was weak.
rows.anchor: cihânı görmez oldu. Veya bir rivayette vârid olduğuna göre zayıf görüyordu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kazīm describes Jacob as containing his distress and anger, swallowing grief, and remaining full of pain.
rows.anchor: derdini içine atıyor, gayzını tutuyor, gam yutuyordu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sons’ admonition is not malicious, but assumes Joseph is dead and implies a hopeless protest; it is an ignorant, disrespectful rebuke to a great and sensitive man.
rows.anchor: Yûsuf’u ölmüş farz etmek gibi bir ye’se ibtinâ ettiği ve bir itiraz ve intikādı tazammun eylediği cihetle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite their rebuke, Jacob responds gently and says he complains of his distress and grief only to God, not to his sons or anyone else.
rows.anchor: ben dedi, bessimi ve hüznümü ancak Allah’a şikâyet ederim ne size ne başkalarına değil.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bess literally means spreading; as a noun for what is spread, it is an overwhelming, heart-rending anguish that one cannot keep inside.
rows.anchor: aslında yaymak, bast u neşr etmek mânasına masdar ise de bundan “mebsûs” mânasıyla isim de olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob knows from God what his sons do not, so they should not think his hope futile; God can bring relief from an unexpected direction.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh bunları boşuna zannetmeyiniz, Allah hiç umulmadık yerden neş’eler verir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taḥassus is an active search for news, using all one’s senses to investigate Joseph and Benjamin.
rows.anchor: bir haber hissetmek için bütün havâssınızla çalışınız, araştırınız.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob does not tell the eldest son, who stayed by choice and was already investigating; Joseph is missing and Benjamin is effectively captive, with no knowledge that either has died.
rows.anchor: büyük kardeşlerinden tehassüs emretmemiştir. Çünkü o ihtiyârıyla kalmış idi, tehassüs üzere bulunuyordu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier claim that a wolf ate Joseph was a lie: an intact shirt shows he could not have been eaten, and Jacob is reported to have called it a very patient wolf.
rows.anchor: Zira gömleği parçalamadan bir kimseyi kurt yemiş olamazdı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Searching for a missing or captive person whose death is unknown and offering possible help is an obligation; failure to search for Joseph had deeply burdened Jacob.
rows.anchor: bir vecîbe teşkil ediyordu ve anlaşılıyor ki Yûsuf hakkında iyi bir tehassüste bulunulmaması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Benjamin’s detention now provides an occasion to investigate both brothers, something Jacob had long wanted the others to do.
rows.anchor: Bünyamin’in tevkīfi yüzünden bir tâkip ve tehassüs lüzûmunun zuhûru ile bu kere o vesile hâsıl olmuştu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rūḥ of God means His relieving grace that opens hardship and lets constricted hearts breathe; only disbelievers despair of it, so they must search hopefully and may return with good news.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın revhinden ümidi kesmeyin yani darlıkları açacak, sıkılmış sînelere nefes aldırıp ferah verecek lutf u rahmetinden ye’se düşmeyin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their words show a profound awakening and new tenderness; Benjamin’s detention completed the remorse, sincerity, and humility that Joseph’s chastisement was meant to produce, so the time had come to reveal himself.
rows.anchor: o ta‘zîr ile gözettiği tevbe ve ihlâs u tevâzu hissi husul bulmuştu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the bearer of good news placed the shirt over Jacob’s face, his sight immediately returned.
rows.anchor: Ya‘kūb’un basarı yerine geliverdi, gözü açılıverdi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob remains composed in beautiful patience and recalls his counsel not to despair of God’s relief (12:87), repeating that he knows from God what the others do not.
rows.anchor: o yine sabr-ı cemîlinden ayrılmayıp وَلَا تَا۟يْـَٔسُوا۟ مِن رَّوْحِ ٱللَّهِ nasihatini ihtar ederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s question points the sons to God’s greatness and the truth of prophethood.
rows.anchor: Yani şimdi anladınız mı Allah ne büyük ve Peygamberlik ne hakikat?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sons confess real guilt and remorse and ask Jacob to pray that their sins be forgiven.
rows.anchor: biz hakikaten suçlu idik şimdi çok nâdim olduk.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob promises to seek forgiveness later rather than immediately, perhaps waiting for an accepted time such as the last part of the night or Friday night.
rows.anchor: istiğfârını seher vakti veya cuma gecesi gibi bir vakt-i icâbet gözettiği için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More precisely, Jacob delays until reconciliation with Joseph or assurance that Joseph has forgiven them, since an oppressed person’s forgiveness is a condition of divine forgiveness.
rows.anchor: daha doğrusu Yûsuf’la helalleştirinceye veya onun affını anlayıncaya kadar tehir etmişti. Çünkü mazlûmun affı mağfiretin şartıdır.
